quotes.text: It's the industry standard for container orchestration, but Kubernetes solves one problem and creates another. Running it yourself is complex.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures in one line why managed Kubernetes services exist.

quotes.text: AKS is the landlord. Microsoft handles the foundation, the control plane, networking, security patches, and upgrades. You bring the furniture, your containerized applications, configurations, and deployment pipelines.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the shared responsibility split in AKS with a memorable analogy.

quotes.text: Then we get down to pod security, which is where most container vulnerabilities happen. The number one rule, do not run containers as root.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the most important pod hardening rule clearly.

quotes.text: Secrets are the next big one. Never store passwords, API keys or connection strings in your code or container images.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete security recommendation that applies to every container workload.

quotes.text: If you have a simple monolithic application running on a single VM, AKS adds complexity without much benefit. You'd be managing Kubernetes just for the sake of managing it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers honest guidance on when not to use AKS.

chapters.title: Costs and when to use AKS

takeaways: AKS is managed Kubernetes: Microsoft runs and patches the control plane, while you choose, scale and pay for the worker node virtual machines.
Plan subnet sizes for growth from day one and secure clusters in layers with Entra ID and Kubernetes RBAC, private clusters, Azure Policy and Key Vault for secrets.
Most AKS cost comes from worker nodes, so right-size them, use the cluster autoscaler, reservations or spot VMs, and avoid AKS for simple monolithic apps.
hook: Kubernetes is the industry standard for running containers, but operating it yourself is a full-time job. This plain-English episode is for developers and IT pros new to containers: it walks through what Azure Kubernetes Service manages for you, from the control plane to nodes, networking and security, plus what it really costs and the pitfalls to avoid.
